name: Traefik
description: Cloud-native HTTP reverse proxy and load balancer.
summary: Traefik welcomes AI-assisted code and documentation contributions, but substantial AI use must be declared with an Assisted-by trailer in the PR description, and anything larger than a bug fix needs maintainer alignment first. AI agents may not author commits, post issue or PR comments or review replies, or submit unvalidated security reports, and AI-drafted messages must be rewritten in the contributor's own voice.

evidence.quote: Traefik welcomes AI-assisted contributions, provided a few simple rules are followed:

**Declare substantial AI assistance in the pull request description**, with `Assisted-by: <agent name>` (for example `Assisted-by: Claude Opus 4.6`), whenever an agent produced a meaningful portion of the diff. Trivial edits such as a typo fix or a one-line rename do not need it.
**Align with a maintainer before generating code for anything larger than a bug fix.**
Open an issue, state the intended approach, and wait for confirmation before asking an agent to implement it.
Never add `Co-authored-by:`, `Assisted-by:` or any other AI attribution trailer to commit messages, and never make an agent the author of a commit.

Three requirements that are easy to miss, all on the policy page: a **working proof of concept with reproduction steps**, **one finding per report**, and **disclose your use of AI tooling**. Unvalidated AI-generated reports are closed immediately.

**Keep issue and PR conversations human.** Do not let an agent post comments, review replies, or triage messages on your behalf. If an agent drafted a message for you, rewrite it in your own voice before sending — maintainers need to know they are talking to a person, not a bot.
